items.title: Generate catalog.json (the single source of truth for atom-aware tooling)
items.detail: Add scripts/build-catalog.mjs, run from `prepare`. For each atom and molecule it emits: tag, PascalName, tier (atom|molecule), frameworks[] (detected from which adapter files exist), props[] with enums (taken from controllers and src/core types such as ComponentSize, SemanticStatus and ComponentVariant), emits[], slots[], and import subpath per framework. Hand-annotated per-component atom.meta.json files supply `replaces` (for example x-btn replaces v-btn and button), `aliases` (a-button, AtomButton), `propMap` (sm/md/lg to small/default/large; ghost to variant=text; danger to color=error; tone to color; open to modelValue; removable to closable), and `safe1to1`. Export the result as `@chemx/x-atoms/catalog` (JSON). Controllers and TS types are the source of truth for props; adapters only signal which frameworks are supported. A spec fails when the catalog is stale.
items.acceptance: (1) `node scripts/build-catalog.mjs` writes dist/catalog.json with 18 or more atoms and 10 or more molecules. x-menu reports frameworks ['vue'] until it gets ports. (2) Every Vue export in src/vue.ts appears in the catalog, enforced by a spec. (3) catalog-sync.spec fails if dist/catalog.json differs from a fresh generation. (4) `import catalog from '@chemx/x-atoms/catalog' with {type:'json'}` resolves in Node. (5) The entry for x-btn includes replaces ['v-btn','button'] and sizes ['x-small','small','default','large','x-large'].

Port the 5 template regexes in extended-text-patterns.js to the AST, keeping the regexes as a fallback when the compilers are missing. Make RAW_INLINE_STYLE fire on Vue `style` and `:style`. Either implement RENDER_TREE_DEPTH_EXCEEDED using the profile's maxRenderDepth, reusing structural-weight.js measureJsxDepth for JSX and the template tree for SFCs, or delete it from the registry and from AGENTS.md section A. Export a `getTemplateTree(file, code)` API for WS-C rules.

items.detail: Add cli/audit/fixtures.spec.js. Seed the should-not-fire files from confirmed real false positives. The studio has 108 ACard and 90 AText uses, and t-social-layout.vue has 6 nested ACards. DESIGN_TOKEN_HARDCODED_COLOR scans .scss files and <style> blocks, but only when a token catalog is loaded (catalog tokens, or a project token file named in .chemxrc so the studio's own palette can be the reference). It reports the nearest token by deltaE and the suggested variable. Feed both rules into the styling-hygiene pillar, which today passes without checking .scss.

The file rotates at 1 MB and `chemx init` gitignores it. `chemx friction --top [--json]` ranks rows by kind and key. `--to-team` creates deduplicated swarm tasks.
items.acceptance: (1) An unknown-action MCP call appends {ts, kind:'unknown_action', action, root}. (2) A Bash command carrying the bypass comment logs kind:'bypass' with the reason. (3) The text output of `chemx friction --top` is 15 lines or fewer. (4) A secret-like token in a command is redacted (spec). (5) Running --to-team twice creates no duplicate tasks.

items.title: Warm socket fast path for hooks
items.detail: The running MCP server, or `chemx daemon`, listens on .chemx/run/chemx.sock with mode 0600 and serves JSON-line operations (check, status, atoms, pre-tool). hosts/claude/bin/chemx-hook.mjs imports only node:net, node:fs and node:path, tries the socket with a 200 ms connect timeout, and otherwise spawns `chemx agent-hook`. The daemon reports its version and file mtimes, and the client restarts it on mismatch. Windows stays disabled until named pipes are tested.
items.acceptance: (1) With the server running, post-edit on a 300-line .vue file completes in under 500 ms p50 over 20 runs (bench spec). (2) Without the socket, the JSON output is identical (parity spec). (3) Stale sockets are detected and replaced, and the socket is removed on exit.
items.files: cli/host/socket-server.js (new), cli/mcp/server.js (start listener), hosts/claude/bin/chemx-hook.mjs (new), cli/host/socket.spec.js (new)

items.title: Literal search recall and index staleness
items.detail: Literal `q -g` scans only indexed files, and the index skips cli/ (search-db.js:55). `q -g process.cwd -l` returns 1 file where rg finds 117, and `starshipDarkTheme` returns nothing from the x-atoms submodule. Change literal mode to walk the gitignore-aware file list used by `chemx f` (or use rg when installed) and resolve paths against the index root, not process.cwd(). Always report scannedFiles, scope and source. Stamp the index with HEAD and the newest mtime, and warn or resync when it is stale. Make `read --symbol` resolve through the index def lookup from importing files. NOTE: cli/search.js, cli/search.spec.js and cli/search-commands-semantic.js have uncommitted user changes. Start from them (commit or stash with the user's consent first) and never discard them.
items.acceptance: (1) search-recall.spec builds a fixture corpus (.js, .ts, .vue, .svelte, .html, a nested submodule and a gitignored dir) and asserts that `q -g X -l` matches `git grep -l X` for 20 needles. (2) --json includes scannedFiles, scope and source, and the text output never prints 'No literal matches' without saying what scope was searched. (3) Touching a file after indexing makes the next q report stale or resync. (4) `chemx read cli/ui-handlers.js --symbol=calculateSavings` resolves to ui-actions-helpers.js.
items.files: cli/search.js, cli/search-commands.js, cli/search-db.js, cli/search-queries.js, cli/reader (read --symbol path), cli/search-recall.spec.js (new)

items.title: `chemx check --since=<rev>` delta mode and honest unanalyzed output
items.detail: Audit `git show <rev>:<file>` alongside the working copy, and report only new violations, keyed by rule plus a normalized snippet. Fall back to per-rule count deltas when keys collide. Line-budget crossings count as new violations. Never print 'Crystalline' for a file the analyzers skip. Return analyzed:false with a reason instead, for example `src/ui/index.html` now gives 0 hazards in 1 ms. WS-E's post-edit hook and WS-C's atomHints consume this.
items.acceptance: (1) On a fixture file with 5 existing violations plus 1 new one, `check --since=HEAD --json` reports exactly 1. (2) Shifting lines above an existing violation does not make it count as new. (3) Going from 99 to 101 lines reports a line-budget crossing. (4) `chemx check src/ui/index.html --json` returns analyzed:false.
items.files: cli/search-commands.js (handleCheckCommand), cli/audit/delta.js (new), cli/audit/delta.spec.js (new)
